problem_mechanism.name: UMP Mechanism 1 — The Velocity Drop
problem_mechanism.plain: The nervous system encodes movement patterns at the speed they actually occur, not the speed intended. When fatigue drops a sprint from 100% to ~70% velocity, the body records the slow speed and installs it as the new default. Training harder/longer actively programs slower movement — 'anti-training', negative adaptation in proportion to fatigued reps.
problem_mechanism.epiphany: Muscle memory remembers the speed, not just the move. The tired reps are rehearsing slow.
problem_mechanism.reframe_of_blame: It's not the kid (not lazy) and not the parent (not negligent) — it's the unmeasured rep / the training method.
problem_mechanism.solution_fix: Principle 3 — SPEED protected: the instant velocity drops 10% below the set's fastest rep, the set ends. No 'two more.' Every rep stays fast. 'The set ending is not the interruption of training — it is the training.'

microscripts_dsi1_grind_trap.dsi: Conventional youth speed training doesn't just fail to develop faster athletes — it actively programs slower movement patterns into the nervous system. Every rep past the velocity-drop threshold teaches the body to move slowly.

metaphors_in_scope.name: The Tired Recording
metaphors_in_scope.gist: Nervous system is a recording device; it records the speed that actually happened. Tired reps write data to the wrong file.

metaphors_in_scope.name: The Wrong Groove (vinyl)
metaphors_in_scope.gist: Every rep at a speed carves a groove; tired reps carve a slow groove that becomes the default under pressure.

metaphors_in_scope.name: Slow Code / Wrong Software
metaphors_in_scope.gist: Tired reps write slow code; output is determined by what's written, not effort applied.

metaphors_in_scope.name: The Drain
metaphors_in_scope.gist: There's a drain at the bottom of every program that doesn't monitor velocity — paying to fill a tank with a hole.

metaphors_in_scope.name: The Grind Trap
metaphors_in_scope.gist: A trap set by grind culture; the path that looks right (work harder, push through) is the trap for explosive speed.

paradoxes_in_scope.text: Why does a child who works harder than everyone — never quits, runs every extra rep — still get slower while a child who does fewer reps at full velocity keeps getting faster?
Why do the most dedicated athletes — most sessions, never skip — plateau the fastest and most completely?
Why is the most celebrated coaching phrase ('push through it') the precise instruction that encodes the opposite of what the coach wants?
Why does a program running 40% more total reps produce 224% worse speed outcomes than one that stops each set early?

voc_quotes.text: I have a deep love for my son and I'm committed to helping him succeed, even if he appears to be moving in slow motion on the field.
'I'm not as good as the rest of my team and I'm scared I'll mess up.' (child)

cost_of_inaction.text: Every month the window is open and the method is wrong is a month that can't be recovered. After PHV you correct patterns instead of forming them — longer, costlier, less complete.

Sliding scale of regret: age 10 'wrong program one season' → age 13 'three years in programs that couldn't measure velocity' → age 16 'remedial pattern work on a post-pubescent body, twice as long, still behind'
'One month here versus three months on a travel team. One produces measurable results. The other produces hotel receipts.'
